note: Source of truth for the build lane. Rendered into BACKLOG.md by tools/render_readme.py. Scores follow RUBRIC.md section 2.

items.title: Spend policy engine for agent-initiated payments
items.thesis: Agents can now check out on their own. Nobody can show you the policy layer that decides whether they should.
items.notes: Closest to the existing ACP POC. Ship after the ACP repo has a distinct angle so this reads as a layer, not a repeat.

items.title: Settlement reconciliation that balances to zero
items.thesis: Every payments team claims their recon is tight. Here is one that scores its own accuracy against injected breaks.
items.notes: First artifact. Break classes are injected with ground truth, so precision and recall are measured, not asserted.

items.title: Agent-to-agent credit with exposure limits and netting
items.thesis: If agents transact with each other all day, someone has to underwrite the float between them.
items.notes: Strongest novelty candidate. Needs a careful failure model: default, exposure, netting window.

items.title: Idempotency conformance suite for payment APIs
items.thesis: A payments API is not idempotent until a buyer can replay it and get the same answer. Most cannot.
items.notes: Shipped 2026-11-02, re-scored 4.60. Five implementations of one charge endpoint, 11 checks, named violation codes. store_after passes 6 of 11 with 7 excess charges; reserve passes 11 of 11. Promotion candidate on 4.6, but the HTTP adapter is what makes it useful to a buyer: promote after that.

items.title: Money allocation and FX rounding engine
items.thesis: The penny that goes missing when you split a payment across three parties is a real bug class, not a rounding footnote.
items.notes: Largest remainder allocation, preservation invariant, property based tests with Hypothesis.

items.title: Sanctions screening that cuts false positives
items.thesis: Screening is not a search box. It is entity resolution, and the cost of a false positive is a frozen customer.
items.notes: Shipped 2026-11-04, re-scored 4.60. 2400 customers, 26 entries, 36 injected true matches, 110 namesakes, fixed review budget. At 48 reviews: name-only caught 11 of 36 and spent 36 reviews on namesakes; entity resolution caught 33 with 11 namesakes and no ranking loss. 130 customers tie at the top name score, so the baseline queue is decided by a tie break. Three customers listed only under a kunya are missed by every policy, which caps recall at 0.917.

items.title: Authorization-rate aware payment routing
items.thesis: Routing on cost alone leaves money on the table. Routing on approval probability is where the margin is.
items.notes: Simulator with PSP-level latency, cost, and approval curves. Compare static rules, epsilon greedy, and Thompson sampling. Shipped 2026-11-06, re-scored 4.60. 50,000 synthetic transactions, 12 segments, hidden per-segment approval. Fee-only routing: 88.9% auth, 124.4 bps, $38,271 per 1,000. Reference: 94.3% auth, 151.3 bps, $39,802 (+4.0%). A three-line rule table recovers 4.06%, Thompson lands 0.06% below the reference, epsilon greedy 0.9% below. After a 0.90 logit shift against bravo on debit, rules lose 0.90% and all-history Thompson 1.25% against the reference, a 300 attempt window is level. Retry depth moves the gap from $2,689 to $1,151.

items.title: Subscription mandate simulator across rails
items.thesis: Card mandates, SEPA direct debit, and UPI autopay disagree about notifications, retries, and revocation. Most teams learn this in production.
items.notes: Shipped 2026-10-26, re-scored 4.75. Promotion candidate: the cross rail claim survives without the lab, but the UPI category exemptions need modelling first.

items.title: Chargeback representment state machine
items.thesis: Every dispute is a clock. The product is knowing which clock is running and what evidence still matters.
items.notes: Shipped 2026-11-11, re-scored 4.75, promotion candidate. 2,000 synthetic disputes, $356,862 disputed, $277,708 (77.8%) defensible, 40 analyst minutes a day. Ladder of five policies: status_only 21.3%, response_clock 66.5%, frees_added 73.8%, complete_evidence 77.3%, three_clock 94.0% ($260,905). Unlimited analyst time reaches 98.2%, so the staffing constraint is worth $11,682 and the queue ordering is worth more. 621 free wins ($153,411, 55.2% of the ceiling) need no evidence; the status tracker captured 6.4% of that. 563 of its 804 forfeits are fraud, because a 25 day sweep is longer than the 20 day fraud window. Contest precision 0.53 to 0.96, wasted minutes 2,385 to 934. All six bench checks pass, including budget and deadline binding checks.

items.title: Broker order, fill, and position reconciliation
items.thesis: Retail trading apps fail quietly at the seam between the broker, the exchange, and the books.
items.notes: Extends the Angel One repo into a reconciliation harness. Keep separate from recon to avoid theme repetition. Shipped 2026-11-09, re-scored 4.70, promotion candidate. 1,200 orders, 1,668 prints, 286 injected breaks in 8 classes. broker_only leaves 844 shares and 27.2 lakh rupees of drift and reports nothing; broker_vs_app flags 206 items at 0.43 precision and still leaves 1,424 shares off; stream_replay leaves 1,779 shares and 5.54 lakh of cash. tape_three_way names all 286 and the reconstructed book equals the tape, with the explained delta equality holding at a max gap of 0 across 6 symbols. Triage at 60 tickets covers 87 percent of rupee exposure by impact, 26 percent by arrival order.

items.title: Append only ledger with a provable close
items.thesis: Closing the books is a testable property, not a monthly meeting.
items.notes: Temporal queries, reversal only, period locks. Overlaps recon, sequence it after.

items.title: LLM underwriting judged by calibration, not vibes
items.thesis: An underwriting model is good when its probabilities mean something. Brier score does not care how confident the prompt sounded.
items.notes: Needs a pinned model and a recorded fixture set so results stay reproducible offline.

items.title: PAN vault with scoped detokenization
items.thesis: Storing the card number is easy. Proving who was allowed to read it, and why, is the product.
items.notes: Useful but the public version is well covered by vendor docs. Low novelty.

items.title: Bank statement to normalized ledger
items.thesis: Turning messy statements into clean entries is the unglamorous tax on every finance product.
items.notes: Crowded space, extraction quality is hard to prove without real statements, and real statements are PII.

items.title: Regulatory change watcher for PSD3, RBI, MiCA
items.thesis: Regulation moves monthly. Most teams read about it when a partner asks.
items.notes: Better as a newsletter than a repo. Fails the measured gate without an evaluation set.

items.title: Confirmation depth priced by ticket, not copied from a doc
items.thesis: A confirmation count is a bet on the depth of the next reorg, priced in blocks and settled in dollars.
items.notes: Shipped 2026-11-16, re-scored 4.75, promotion candidate. 4,000 synthetic stablecoin payments a week, USD 1.67M per week, four held out weeks and USD 6.69M scored per policy. Credit on inclusion: 366 false credits, USD 84,791.45 lost, 136.4 bps. Fixed 12: USD 13,912.83, 22.4 bps, 26 seconds median wait, and USD 13,857.15 of it on the fast chain. Per chain defaults of 12, 30 and 32: USD 13,857.15, 61 seconds median, USD 55.68 avoided. Ticket tiers: USD 2,832.36, 4.6 bps, 92.5 percent inside 60 seconds. Calibrated on 28 days of another seed: USD 202.64, 0.3 bps, 93 seconds median. The fixed depth sweep is a cliff: k=12 USD 13,913, k=24 USD 8,258, k=32 USD 6,608, k=40 USD 359, k=48 USD 0. Stress with incidents 1.5x deeper than the calibration month: calibrated USD 6,740 against USD 5,322 for the tier table, so the fitted curve is the cheapest in distribution and the less robust out of it. 58 tests, gate green at 1450 python lines. Promotion needs real chain headers for the loss curve, not another generator.

items.title: Consent refresh timed against the debit, not the calendar
items.thesis: An A2A payment rides on an authorisation that expires, so every renewal is a chance for the customer to leave. The timing of the ask decides which loss you take.
items.notes: Queue was empty, so this was scored and built in the same run. Shipped 2026-11-18, re-scored 4.35. 1,200 payers, 13,834 scheduled debits, USD 525,635.54 billed, 90 day consent lifetime. fixed_30 captured 51.0%, never_refresh 28.3%, fixed_90 73.8%, on_failure 66.0%, jit_1 80.3%, jit_2 88.2%, jit_3 89.7%, jit_7 84.8%, adaptive 86.3%. The sweep is a cliff at the context window: lead 3 captures 89.7% with 100% of prompts near a debit, lead 4 drops to 83.2% with 0%. Stress without the contextual advantage flips the winner to jit_7. 27 tests, gate green at 1108 python lines.

items.title: Intraday liquidity buffer sized against the settlement clock
items.thesis: A daily net position says the account funds itself. The 11:00 payout run says otherwise, and the buffer between them is a measured number, not a policy preference.
items.notes: Queue was empty, so this was scored and built in the same run. Shipped 2026-11-18, scored 4.75, promotion candidate. 720 synthetic business days, USD 1,369,861,695 of payouts, cumulative net flow USD 9,881. Required opening: mean USD 1,294,716, p90 USD 1,655,285, worst day USD 3,079,874. zero buffer USD 448,355 a year, daily_net_p95 USD 271,703 with 95.6 percent of days short, gross_batch USD 140,727, peak_p90 USD 106,970 with 84 failed batches, peak_p100 USD 137,985, oracle USD 71,127. All 393 net positive days short at a zero buffer. Settlement at 08:00 instead of 16:30 cuts the p90 float to USD 305,080 and the best policy to USD 33,638. The batch split regime is an exact null: 45/55 and 60/40 give the same requirement to the cent. Trailing window from 20 to 160 days lands within 1.1 percent. 37 tests, gate green at 1344 python lines.

items.title: Capture windows matched to merchant class, not to the calendar
items.thesis: An authorisation is a promise with a deadline. One window for a whole merchant book loses money on both sides of that date, and the window that fits is a property of the merchant class.
items.notes: Queue was empty: every hardening item was shipped and the backlog held no queued idea, so this was scored and built in the same run. Shipped 2026-11-19, re-scored 4.65. 2,500 synthetic authorisations over 170 days, 2,967 settlement requests, USD 383,504.17 requested, USD 9,271.24 of tips above the authorisation, 193 never settled. The 7 day window captured 59.1% and refused USD 116,883.23, which is 30.48% of the book, matching the 30.5% of value that arrives after day 7. 14 days 86.5%, 21 days 88.6%, 28 days 89.6% with zero expiry refusals and USD 4,715,738.70 of frozen funds days against USD 2,140,155.70 at 7 days. Tiered windows (7 restaurant and retail, 14 multi item, 21 hotel and late batch) captured the same 88.6% as a blanket 21 days with 16.75% fewer funds days. Over limit handling: refusing the whole capture lost USD 40,028.52 against USD 1,866.14 for settling what fits, 21.45 times, and 4.32 times the whole tip book. Tolerance 0% and 5% print identical rows because every tipped capture is refused outright below the smallest tip rate: a plateau, stated as such. 24 tests, gate green at 988 python lines. S2 scored 4, not 5, because the invariant is proven but error classes are not measured as precision and recall.

items.title: Card fee qualification gap and repair ranking
items.thesis: The merchant negotiates the rate and pays for the missing field. Card fees are rate times qualification, and qualification is auditable.
items.notes: Queue was empty: every backlog item was shipped or parked and every hardening item was shipped, so this was scored and built in the same run. Shipped 2026-11-20, scored 4.65. 61,985 synthetic transactions over 45 days, USD 11,174,093.62 processed. Billed USD 255,120.61, fully qualified USD 204,734.23, gap USD 50,386.38 (45.09 bps of value, 19.75% of the bill), 28,553 transactions with a gap. Partition by binding rule: commercial_data USD 29,420.29 (58.4%), avs_cvv USD 9,133.38, unauthorized USD 5,367.07, commercial_l3 USD 2,942.57, mcc_mismatch USD 1,943.35, late_batch USD 1,292.51, stored_credential USD 287.21. Best single commercial_data USD 20,451.98 (40.6%). Best pair commercial_data plus avs_cvv USD 30,485.41 (60.5%), 5.455 times a 5 bps cut of USD 5,588.58. Best triple adds commercial_l3, USD 37,908.13 (75.2%). Sum of singles USD 36,361.28, so USD 14,025.10 of the gap sits behind a higher failure. The lowest rule can never be masked, pinned in a test. Stress at 0.4x missing field rates: gap USD 23,674.48, 10.37% of the bill, same pair wins at 66.3%. 28 tests, gate green at 1155 python lines.

items.title: SCA exemption selection priced against the fraud rate it moves
items.thesis: The exemption ladder is a control, not an entitlement: the ceiling a merchant may use depends on the fraud the exemptions at that ceiling produce, and that rate is measured over every remote card payment.
items.notes: Queue was empty: every backlog item was shipped or parked and every hardening item was shipped, so this was scored and built in the same run. Shipped 2026-11-23, scored 4.50. 49,752 synthetic remote card transactions over 60 days, EUR 2,953,266.79 processed, latent fraud 14.16 bps. Challenge all EUR 34,942.88, of which 99.1 percent is friction. Exempt everything EUR 4,710.16 and 56 of 60 days over the 1 bp reference rate, worst window 29.98 bps. Best compliant policy (one rung down, risk cutoff 0.12) EUR 25,026.14, 27.5 percent of value exempt, 0 breach days, saves EUR 10,217.70 of friction for EUR 300.96 of added fraud, 28.4 percent off challenge all. Ladder at its ceiling with a risk test EUR 16,439.13 with 8 breach days, worst window 4.91 bps over 6. Compliance premium over the unconstrained floor EUR 20,315.98, 4.3 times the floor. The article 16 counters refused 61 of 14,152 under-cap transactions, so the EUR 30 cap is what binds there. 31 tests, gate green at 979 python lines. Promotion candidate for the recap lane.

items.title: ATM cash replenishment priced by trip, by balance, and by service
items.thesis: A machine is a stock with a flow problem: the cadence and the fill quantity have opposite costs, and the default of one trip a week filled to the top is dominated on both.
items.notes: Queue was empty: every backlog item was shipped or parked and every hardening item was shipped, so this was scored and built in the same run. Shipped 2026-11-25, scored 4.05. 60 synthetic machines, 120 days, 898,883 withdrawals, 6,144,545 notes, INR 3,072,272,500. Weekly full fill INR 7,684,571.80 at 99.423 percent service and 21.48 bps of value; daily min/max INR 6,597,770.30 at 100 percent, 16.47 percent cheaper and 0.577 points better. Same trips with a seven day fill frees INR 987,164.28 of funding and loses 36,517 withdrawals. Fortnightly trips cut CIT 40.73 percent and end 39.49 percent more expensive with 25.39 percent of withdrawals unserved. Fixed cadence capacity sweep 74.935, 94.691, 99.423, 99.943, 99.998 percent for two to six cassettes; 99.5 percent needs five cassettes at INR 9,676,489.65, 46.66 percent above the daily policy. Any day trips serve 100 percent at every rung, so capacity is a cost choice unless the schedule is fixed. Oracle gap INR 778,651.59, 11.8 percent. 98.84 percent of the weekly policy's lost withdrawals are metro. 35 tests, gate green at 1183 python lines, both results files re-derived by tools/repro.py. S7 scored 3: cash logistics is adjacent to the lab thesis, not core to it, so this is not a promotion candidate.

items.title: Correspondent charge codes priced by what the beneficiary receives
items.thesis: The charge code does not change what the chain takes, only who pays it, so the code that looks cheapest on your own ledger is the one that puts the shortfall on your supplier.
items.notes: Queue was empty: every backlog item was shipped or parked and every hardening item was shipped, so this was scored and built in the same run. Shipped 2026-11-26, scored 4.65, promotion candidate. 2,000 synthetic supplier invoices over 90 days, USD 12,138,953 instructed across five corridors of one to three hops, median ticket USD 4,200. The chains take USD 47,499.41, 39.13 bps. SHA costs the payer 29.75 bps and leaves the beneficiary 39.13 bps short, 68.88 in total; OUR costs 61.20 with nothing deducted, so SHA is 31.45 bps cheaper on the payer's ledger and 7.68 bps, USD 9,320, dearer in total. BEN is the cheapest row on the payer's ledger at 16.82 bps and the second worst policy at 73.43, because it puts the sender bank's fee on the supplier too. Repairing every claim costs 92.72 bps, 31.52 bps above the bundle: the median claim is USD 37, the minimum wire fee is USD 35, and the average repaired claim costs USD 105.21 including the USD 37 owed. The claim threshold sweep is a staircase from 92.72 at USD 25 to 68.88 at USD 250 and never, and the largest claim on the book is USD 100.08, so every threshold above it is the same policy. The tolerated deduction is the free lever: USD 25 to USD 50 cuts claims from 827 to 189 and total cost from 68.88 to 59.42 bps, USD 11,483, because those shortfalls were already being absorbed. A tolerance below the smallest lift, USD 12, behaves as zero, which is why the first two rungs print identically. OUR wins on two and three hop corridors and above USD 5,475 to USD 10,875 depending on the route; a per corridor rule reaches 56.41 bps, 56.67 percent of the oracle prize of USD 26,713.23, while an expected-deduction rule reaches only 12.54 percent and loses to the blunt bundle. 46 tests, gate green at 1350 python lines, both results files re-derived by tools/repro.py.

items.title: Seller payout reserves priced against the hold and the risk band
items.thesis: A reserve and a hold are two prices on the same refund risk, and the cheaper one is not the one most platforms use.
items.notes: Queue was empty: every backlog item was shipped or parked and every hardening item was shipped, so this was scored and built in the same run. Shipped 2026-11-27, scored 4.55, promotion candidate. 400 synthetic sellers, 180 days, 52,349 orders, USD 6,927,844.81 GMV, 1,932 refunds costing USD 254,124.66. Pay T+1 writes off USD 57,605.04, 22.7 percent of the refund book, 263 sellers. A 15 percent reserve held 30 days cuts it to USD 21,835.52 for USD 12,329.06 of float, 50.2 bps against 86.4, capturing 49.8 percent of the perfect foresight prize. A 14 day hold writes off USD 33,537.86 for USD 31,813.71 of float, dominated by a 10 percent reserve at USD 25,911.97 and USD 8,879.54, and every hold rung is worse in total than T+1. Reserve marginal net turns negative at 20 percent: 15 to 20 spends USD 3,442.10 to save USD 1,980.62. Banding new and risky sellers halves the write-off and still costs USD 57,605.53, USD 23,440.95 above the blunt reserve, because established sellers are 70 percent of the book, 89.7 percent of GMV and 61.6 percent of write-off dollars. Clawback is worth USD 2,250.32. Three seeds, same 15 percent winner, 43.0 to 49.8 percent of the prize. 43 tests, gate green at 1323 python lines, both results files re-derived by tools/repro.py.

items.title: Deposit sweep priced in yield, insurance, and operational links
items.thesis: A sweep engine that maximises yield leaves the tail uninsured. Capping it costs no yield when capacity binds, and the real bill is the customer to bank links.
items.notes: Queue was empty: every backlog item was shipped or parked and every hardening item was shipped, so this was scored and built in the same run. Shipped 2026-11-28, scored 4.15. 1,500 synthetic customers, USD 50,410,003.08 of deposits, 8 partner banks at 3.40 to 4.55 percent with USD 55,000,000 of capacity, seven banks full, 91.65 percent of capacity used. The yield-only default leaves USD 1,162,238.27 uninsured, 2.30 percent of the book, on 10 customers, all of it on 11 balances above the cap. Three links cuts it to USD 133,344.23, 0.26 percent, for 12 links and USD 18.00, and earns the same USD 1,910,440.10, because capacity sets the blended rate: doubling capacity adds USD 137,525.01, 7.20 percent, 27 bps. Four links is zero uninsured at USD 19.50 a year. Equal split across 8 banks also reaches zero with 5,088 links against 1,520, 3.35 times, USD 5,352.00 a year more. Order changes no interest and changes uninsured by USD 1,051,969.52: smallest first leaves USD 1,185,313.75 exposed and costs the top 10 customers USD 39,238.46, so largest first is the only order that uses the cap where it can bind. Boundary: on a 60 customer book of USD 1,709,408.38 that fits inside the top bank, the cap costs USD 242.32, 1.41 bps. 42 tests, gate green at 1,031 python lines, both results files re-derived by tools/repro.py.
